title: 2 Kings 17
paragraphs: ¹ In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king in Samaria over Israel, and he reigned for nine years. ² He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes, though not as the kings of Israel before him had been. ³ Shalmaneser king of Assyria came against him, and Hoshea became his vassal and paid him tribute. ⁴ But the king of Assyria uncovered a conspiracy by Hoshea: he had sent envoys to So king of Egypt, and he had stopped paying the yearly tribute to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria had him arrested and imprisoned. ⁵ Then the king of Assyria invaded the whole land, advanced on Samaria, and besieged it for three years.

⁶ In Hoshea's ninth year, the king of Assyria captured Samaria and deported the Israelites to Assyria, settling them in Halah and along the Habor River in Gozan, and in the towns of the Medes. ⁷ This happened because the Israelites had sinned against the LORD their God, who had brought them up from Egypt and freed them from the power of Pharaoh king of Egypt. They had worshiped other gods ⁸ and followed the practices of the nations the LORD had driven out before them, as well as the customs introduced by the kings of Israel. ⁹ The Israelites secretly did things against the LORD their God that were not right. They built for themselves high places in all their towns, from the watchtowers to the fortified cities. ¹⁰ They set up sacred stones and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every leafy tree.

¹¹ At every high place they burned incense, as the nations the LORD had driven out before them had done. They did wicked things that provoked the LORD to anger. ¹² They worshiped idols — the very things the LORD had told them, "You must not do this." ¹³ The LORD had warned Israel and Judah through every prophet and seer: "Turn from your evil ways. Observe my commandments and decrees, in accordance with all the Law I commanded your ancestors and delivered to you through my servants the prophets." ¹⁴ But they would not listen. They were as stubborn as their ancestors, who had refused to trust in the LORD their God. ¹⁵ They rejected his decrees and the covenant he had made with their ancestors, and they ignored the warnings he had given them. They chased worthless idols and became worthless themselves, following the nations around them — though the LORD had commanded them not to do as those nations did.

¹⁶ They abandoned all the commandments of the LORD their God. They made two idols cast in the shape of calves, and they made an Asherah pole; they bowed down to all the starry hosts and worshiped Baal. ¹⁷ They sacrificed their sons and daughters in the fire; they practiced divination and sought omens. They sold themselves to do evil in the LORD's eyes, and so provoked his anger. ¹⁸ The LORD was furious with Israel and removed them from his presence. Only the tribe of Judah remained. ¹⁹ Even Judah did not keep the commands of the LORD their God — they followed the practices that Israel had introduced. ²⁰ So the LORD rejected all the people of Israel; he afflicted them and handed them over to plunderers, until at last he cast them from his presence.

²¹ When he had torn Israel away from the house of David, they made Jeroboam son of Nebat their king. Jeroboam drove Israel away from following the LORD and led them into great sin. ²² The Israelites walked in all the sins of Jeroboam and would not give them up ²³ until the LORD finally removed Israel from his presence, as he had declared through all his servants the prophets. So Israel was taken from their own land into exile in Assyria — and they remain there to this day. ²⁴ The king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim and settled them in the towns of Samaria to replace the Israelites. They took possession of Samaria and lived in its towns. ²⁵ When they first settled there, they did not honor the LORD — so the LORD sent lions among them, and the lions killed some of them.

²⁶ Word was sent to the king of Assyria: "The peoples you deported and settled in the towns of Samaria don't know the requirements of the god of that land. He has sent lions among them, and they are killing people because they don't know what that god requires." ²⁷ The king of Assyria ordered, "Send back one of the priests you carried off from Samaria. Let him go and live there and teach the people what the god of the land requires." ²⁸ So one of the priests who had been exiled from Samaria came back and settled in Bethel, teaching the people how to honor the LORD. ²⁹ But each national group kept making its own gods in the towns where they had settled, and they placed these gods in the shrines the Samaritans had made, each group in the town where they lived. ³⁰ The men of Babylon made Succoth-benoth; the men of Cuth made Nergal; the men of Hamath made Ashima;

³¹ the Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak; and the Sepharvites burned their children in the fire as sacrifices to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim. ³² They worshiped the LORD, but they also appointed all sorts of their own people as priests of the high places, who offered sacrifices for them in the shrines. ³³ They worshiped the LORD, but they also served their own gods, following the customs of the nations from which they had been brought. ³⁴ To this day they persist in their old practices. They do not truly worship the LORD, nor do they follow the decrees and ordinances, the laws and commands that the LORD gave to the descendants of Jacob, whom he named Israel. ³⁵ The LORD had made a covenant with them and commanded them: "Do not worship other gods or bow down to them or serve them or sacrifice to them.

³⁶ It is the LORD who brought you out of Egypt with great power and an outstretched arm — him you shall worship, him you shall bow down to, and to him you shall offer sacrifice. ³⁷ And the decrees, the ordinances, the laws, and the commands he wrote for you — you shall always be careful to obey. You must not worship other gods. ³⁸ Do not forget the covenant I made with you, and do not worship other gods. ³⁹ Rather, worship the LORD your God; it is he who will deliver you from all your enemies." ⁴⁰ But they refused to listen. They kept on doing as they had done before.
⁴¹ And so these nations worshiped the LORD, but they also served their carved images. Their children and grandchildren continued doing as their fathers had done — and they do to this day.
